subject.title: revert(openai): remove loopback Codex proxy support

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally withdraw the loopback credential-proxy capability and restore the direct Codex subscription route, after validating the exact sibling Codex runtime contract?
rationale: This is a deliberate removal of recently merged auth and routing behavior; repository policy requires direct Codex-source verification, and neither tests nor the PR description can resolve the supported long-term credential boundary alone.

options.title: Validate and merge the revert
options.body: Inspect the sibling Codex request and account-header contract, run a real restored subscription-path proof, and merge if loopback proxying is not a supported product boundary.

options.title: Retain the proxy feature
options.body: Keep the merged proxy capability if maintainers intend to support local credential brokers, then reopen a narrowly scoped fix only for demonstrated proxy defects.

options.title: Pause for a documented contract
options.body: Hold the revert until the supported OpenAI subscription and local-broker ownership boundary is documented by the responsible owners.

recommendation.title: Validate and merge the revert
recommendation.body: Inspect the sibling Codex request and account-header contract, run a real restored subscription-path proof, and merge if loopback proxying is not a supported product boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the merged feature and its proposed reversion and can clarify the originating requester’s intended provider boundary.
